verdict.left_looks: A tiered pagoda-like wooden tower on a grey stone plinth. Dark brown plank/log walls, a wide lower storey with five window slits and a central door, then stepped roof tiers that narrow upward with small eaves, a short upper cupola with a window slot, and a tall thin antenna-like spire on top. Surfaces are a uniform dark brown with little variation; roofs are the same brown as the walls, with no contrasting roof material. The down-the-street views show a stepped, slightly lopsided profile with a sloping stair-stepped side. Clean, simple, few added details.
verdict.right_looks: A larger multi-tier pagoda/temple on a grey mossy stone base with a few flowers and moss patches. Dark wood walls with framed square panel detailing on the lower storey, mixed materials: dark cobble-like grey roof caps on each tier, purple-tinted accent blocks, and small wooden finials and curled eave ornaments at the corners. Two stacked roof tiers with pronounced overhangs, open colonnade with pillars and lanterns at the base, and a tall layered spire with hanging finials. Richer, more ornamented and textured, with visible patina and mixed materials that read as deliberate style.
verdict.why: The right build has a stronger silhouette with layered overhanging roofs, curled eave ornaments, and a more textured mix of wood and stone roof caps that reads as a distinct temple with character, while the left is a plainer, uniform brown stack that looks more like a generic tower; the right's ornament and material variety are deliberate style, not damage.
